headline: High: Devin’s broad cloud-workspace and write/API access can conflict with slim’s privileged container operations, creating dangerous shared-resource and action-cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, Slack, GitHub, Jira, Notion, and MCP outputs by default, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and accepts stdin/stdout commands. If Devin forwards slim-generated text into prompts or parses CLI output as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. The pair lacks a documented isolation bridge, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Devin ingests slim-produced logs, manifests, or command output as trusted instructions
IF a shared workspace or MCP bridge passes slim output into Devin prompts without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from slim logs and artifacts
Add provenance labels to all cross-agent text handoffs
Route slim output through a human review step before Devin consumes it
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted schemas only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and can write to GitHub/Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion; slim touches container images, certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. Because both have broad network egress and filesystem access, a shared workspace or integration path could expose sensitive data externally. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible enough to rate high.
conditions: IF Devin and slim operate on the same repository, workspace, or credential set
IF slim processes images or files containing private keys, env vars, or registry credentials while Devin can read the resulting artifacts or logs
mitigations: Separate credentials and workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from any shared repo or artifact path
Turn off automatic upload of logs/artifacts to external services
Rotate any registry or integration tokens used in the shared environment
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and secret-redaction policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad cloud-workspace shell access; slim can also write the filesystem and execute shell commands, with privileged mode requested. If both target the same directory or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The overlap is direct and dangerous in default-style autonomous operation.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same checkout, container, or mounted volume
IF Devin commits while slim rewrites files or build artifacts in the same path
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Serialize git writes with a lock or single-writer policy
Disable privileged mode for slim unless explicitly needed
Use branch-per-agent workflows with merge review
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file and git locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on outputs, while slim is an interactive CLI that emits analysis of container images and filesystem artifacts. If Devin treats slim’s findings as authoritative, it may propagate incorrect build, security, or deployment actions without verification. The interaction is a classic output-to-action cascade and is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Devin consumes slim reports and then opens PRs, changes configs, or triggers deployments based on them
IF slim outputs are not independently verified before Devin acts
mitigations: Require a second verification step before Devin acts on slim output
Mark slim reports as advisory, not authoritative
Limit Devin to drafting changes rather than executing them automatically
Add checksum or schema validation for slim outputs
requires-engineering: implement policy gates for action-taking based on external tool reports

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, docs, issue trackers, and integration tokens in a vendor-managed cloud workspace; slim handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials inside a temporary container. The profiles show different data classes and retention surfaces, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch. Because compliance gaps are plausible yet undocumented, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets is routed through both agents
IF the operator requires a single retention or residency policy across cloud workspace and temporary container
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents’ shared workflows
Document retention and deletion expectations for each agent
Avoid placing secrets in artifacts that cross the boundary
Review vendor terms for residency and logging
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and data-processing agreements
